subject.name: Geology
subject.description: Grade 11 Semester 1 Geology explores the physical principles and Earth processes that shape landforms, water systems, soils, and the dynamic environment around us. This course connects geology and hydrology by examining water’s role in Earth systems, sediment movement, erosion, deposition, and the interaction between natural processes and human activity.

content.title: Unit 1 (Lo1)
content.description: This unit introduces the extraordinary role of water in shaping Earth’s surface and sustaining life, highlighting why water’s physical and chemical properties make it uniquely important in geology, climate, and the environment.

concepts.title: Abundance of liquid water on Earth’s surface
concepts.description: This concept explains why liquid water is so widespread on Earth and how its abundance supports ecosystems, climate regulation, and geological processes.

concepts.title: Unique combination of physical and chemical properties of water
concepts.description: This concept highlights the unusual properties of water that make it essential for life and geology, including its polarity, hydrogen bonding, and solvent behavior.

concepts.title: Water’s capacity to absorb, store, and release large amounts of energy
concepts.description: This concept explores the thermal buffering role of water and how it stores and transfers energy, helping regulate global temperature and climate.

concepts.title: Water’s ability to transmit sunlight
concepts.description: This concept explains how water allows sunlight to penetrate through it, affecting aquatic environments, photosynthesis, and energy distribution in oceans and lakes.

concepts.title: Expansion of water upon freezing
concepts.description: This concept examines the unusual behavior of water expanding when it freezes and the importance of this property in lakes, rivers, and climate systems.

concepts.title: Water’s ability to dissolve and transport materials
concepts.description: This concept shows how water acts as a solvent and transport medium, moving dissolved minerals and sediments through the geologic and hydrologic cycles.

concepts.title: Water’s ability to lower the viscosities and melting points of rocks
concepts.description: This concept explains how water influences rock behavior by reducing viscosity and melting temperature, which is significant in metamorphic and magmatic processes.

concepts.title: Distribution of Earth’s water: 97% oceans, 3% fresh water
concepts.description: This concept emphasizes the global distribution of water and the small fraction that is available as fresh water for human use and ecosystems.

concepts.title: Fresh water as an important resource
concepts.description: This concept highlights why fresh water is a limited and valuable resource, underscoring its importance for agriculture, industry, human health, and environmental stability.

content.title: Unit 2 (Lo2)
content.description: This unit explores water as a vital Earth resource and examines how water moves through the atmosphere, hydrosphere, and geologic environment while being stored in natural and human-made reservoirs.

concepts.title: Water as a vital Earth resource
concepts.description: This concept explains why water is essential for life, ecosystems, agriculture, industry, and long-term environmental balance on Earth.

concepts.title: Movement of water through the Earth system
concepts.description: This concept introduces the hydrologic cycle and shows how water is continuously circulated between land, oceans, atmosphere, and living organisms.

concepts.title: Storage of water in natural or human-constructed reservoirs
concepts.description: This concept examines how water is stored in rivers, lakes, aquifers, dams, and reservoirs, emphasizing their role in water management and supply.

concepts.title: Surface water reservoirs
concepts.description: This concept describes surface reservoirs such as lakes, rivers, and wetlands and their importance in storage, transport, and ecosystem support.

concepts.title: Groundwater reservoirs
concepts.description: This concept explores underground water stored in aquifers and how groundwater moves, is stored, and is accessed for human use.

content.title: Unit 3 (Lo3)
content.description: This unit investigates how water is transferred between reservoirs and how human societies withdraw, manage, and distribute freshwater resources to meet environmental and economic needs.

concepts.title: Processes that transfer water between stores
concepts.description: This concept explains the movement of water between atmosphere, land, and oceans through precipitation, evaporation, infiltration, runoff, and collection.

concepts.title: Water supplies withdrawn from surface water or groundwater
concepts.description: This concept examines how water is abstracted from rivers, lakes, and aquifers and why careful management is needed to avoid depletion and pollution.

concepts.title: Water management methods
concepts.description: This concept introduces strategies for collecting, storing, regulating, and protecting freshwater resources so they remain usable and sustainable.

concepts.title: Distribution of freshwater resources using
concepts.description: This concept looks at how fresh water is distributed across regions and the challenges involved in ensuring equitable access to this essential resource.

content.title: Unit 4 (Lo4)
content.description: This unit focuses on water pollution and treatment, showing how contaminants enter surface and groundwater systems and how natural and engineered processes can remove pollutants.

concepts.title: Pollutants can contaminate surface water and groundwater
concepts.description: This concept explains how chemicals, waste materials, and human activity can pollute rivers, lakes, aquifers, and groundwater systems.

concepts.title: Surface water generally contains more varied pollutants
concepts.description: This concept describes why surface waters are often more vulnerable to mixed contamination from runoff, industrial discharge, and urban activities.

concepts.title: Water pollutants can be organic or inorganic
concepts.description: This concept distinguishes between organic and inorganic pollutants and explains how each type affects water quality and ecosystem health.

concepts.title: Evaporation as a natural water-purification process
concepts.description: This concept shows how evaporation separates water from dissolved impurities and acts as a natural purification process in the hydrologic cycle.

concepts.title: Condensation as a natural water-purification process
concepts.description: This concept explains how condensation can convert water vapor into cleaner liquid water and how this process contributes to natural purification.

concepts.title: Bacterial activities as a natural water-purification process
concepts.description: This concept examines how microorganisms help break down organic pollutants and improve water quality in natural aquatic environments.

concepts.title: Wastewater treatment involves a series of steps
concepts.description: This concept outlines the sequential processes used in wastewater treatment to remove solids, microbes, and chemical contaminants before water is released or reused.

content.title: Unit 5 (Lo5)
content.description: This unit examines river systems as dynamic channels for water movement, showing how stream networks form, function, and connect to the larger hydrologic cycle and regional drainage basins.

concepts.title: A river system is a network of streams
concepts.description: This concept explains that a river system is made up of connected stream channels that collect and move water and sediment across the landscape.

concepts.title: River systems are important in the hydrologic cycle
concepts.description: This concept shows how rivers redistribute water from land to oceans and contribute to the continuous circulation of water through the Earth system.

concepts.title: River systems consist of different parts
concepts.description: This concept describes the major parts of a river system and how their roles differ depending on location and topography.

concepts.title: Different river-system parts have different forms and functions
concepts.description: This concept explains how upstream, midstream, and downstream sections of a river system differ in shape, sediment load, velocity, and depositional behavior.

concepts.title: Local stream networks create a drainage basin regionally
concepts.description: This concept demonstrates how a network of tributaries and streams defines a drainage basin and how runoff is gathered and directed toward a common outlet.

content.title: Unit 6 (Lo6)
content.description: This unit focuses on river dynamics and landform development, showing how flowing water erodes, transports, and deposits sediment in different stream environments.

concepts.title: Rivers are most effective in causing erosion and deposition of land
concepts.description: This concept explains how rivers shape landscapes by eroding material in some places and depositing sediment in others, creating valleys, channels, and floodplains.

concepts.title: High-gradient streams have different features from low-gradient streams
concepts.description: This concept compares steep, fast-moving streams to low-gradient rivers and explains how slope influences erosion, sediment transport, and channel form.

content.title: Unit 7 (Lo7)
content.description: This unit examines wind as an agent of erosion, transport, and deposition, showing how wind shape changes depend on particle size, wind speed, surface conditions, and sediment availability.

concepts.title: Wind is a major factor creating the physical properties of landforms and human-made features
concepts.description: This concept explains how wind erosion and deposition shape desert landscapes, dunes, and other landforms while also affecting human-made structures and surfaces.

concepts.title: Relationship between particle size and wind speed
concepts.description: This concept shows how the size of sediment particles and the speed of wind determine whether particles are lifted, moved, or deposited.

concepts.title: Factors affecting wind erosion
concepts.description: This concept examines the environmental and physical factors that influence how strongly wind erodes loose sediment and exposed surfaces.

concepts.title: Factors affecting sediment deposition
concepts.description: This concept explores the conditions under which wind-transported particles settle and accumulate to form dunes, loess, and other depositional features.

content.title: Unit 8 (Lo8)
content.description: This unit focuses on soils as the products of weathering, erosion, and deposition, emphasizing the role of soil components in determining texture, fertility, and special soil conditions.

concepts.title: Soils are the final products of different erosional and depositional factors
concepts.description: This concept explains how soil forms from the accumulation and alteration of weathered material under the influence of erosion, transport, and deposition.

concepts.title: Soil contains
concepts.description: This concept examines the main components of soil and how mineral matter, organic matter, water, and air contribute to soil function and composition.

concepts.title: Components of soil occur in varying proportions
concepts.description: This concept highlights that soil properties depend on the relative amounts of mineral grains, organic matter, moisture, and air in the soil profile.

concepts.title: Proportions of soil components determine many physical properties of soil
concepts.description: This concept shows how the balance of soil components affects texture, permeability, fertility, and the soil’s response to water and root growth.

concepts.title: Examples of special soil conditions
concepts.description: This concept introduces unusual soil situations that arise from specific environmental conditions and explains why they differ from typical soils.

concepts.title: Caliche
concepts.description: This concept describes caliche as a hardened mineral deposit often found in arid regions and explains how it forms and affects the soil profile.

concepts.title: Salinized soil
concepts.description: This concept examines salinized soils, showing how salt accumulation reduces fertility and affects agricultural productivity in dry environments.

content.title: Midterms Revisions
content.description: This revision section brings together the major materials, processes, and systems studied in the first half of the course so students can review river, water, and landform concepts before formal assessment.

content.title: Final Revisions
content.description: This final review consolidates the major geological and hydrologic ideas from the course, reinforcing how water, rivers, wind, and soils shape Earth systems and human activity.

content.description: Additional supporting geology and hydrology videos that extend the core learning outcomes and provide extra context for understanding Earth systems.
